messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Scaling problem with geom_density
parts:
The following works fine:

     ggplot(data.frame(x=runif(1000,0,1e6))) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) 

but changing 1e6 -> 1e7 does not; it chooses an inappropriate y range and produces a straight line:

     ggplot(data.frame(x=runif(1000,0,1e7))) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) 

OK, I suppose that's not surprising, and I should be able to scale manually.  But I couldn't get coord and scale to work even in the first (1e6) case:

   ggplot(data.frame(x=runif(1000,0,1e6))) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(5e-7,12e-7))  # bad
   ggplot(data.frame(x=runif(1000,0,1e6))) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) + scale_y_continuous(limits=c(5e-7,12e-7))  #bad

With scale, it appears that the lower limit must be 0:

   ggplot(data.frame(x=runif(1000,0,1e6))) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) + scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,12e-7)) #OK

With coord, the lower limit can be 2e-7, but not 3e-7, which seems awfully arbitrary:

   ggplot(data.frame(x=runif(1000,0,1e6))) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(2e-7,12e-7)) # OK
   ggplot(data.frame(x=runif(1000,0,1e6))) + geom_density(aes(x=x)) + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(3e-7,12e-7)) # not OK

In case you think this is an artificial case, let me assure you that it is actually very real: I was looking at the density of about 100,000 events in a 10-year period, that is, a range of 315360000 seconds (POSIXct).  Using as.Date scaled the data enough that geom_density didn't have a problem.  But I'd think that the absolute scale shouldn't cause problems like this.

            -s

R 2.13.1
ggplot2 0.8.9
